Quick update / artifacts attached.

Summary of technical responses (draft):
- Signals ingested: text-generation request metadata (model, prompt length, token counts), user-provided metadata (if provided by customer), embedding similarity scores (for reranking misuse patterns), anomaly scores from our behavioral model, rate / burst counters, and third-party signals (when integrated via webhook).
- Detection: combination of rule-based heuristics (regex, rate thresholds) + ML anomaly detector trained on traffic baselines; detectors emit alert types: 'policy-violation-suspected', 'credential-extraction-pattern', 'automated-synthetic-abuse'.
- KV/prefix cache retention: customer-configurable TTLs; default ephemeral KV cache retained for 24 hours for routing/streaming performance, with optional 90-day short-term retention for Dedicated customers who opt into audit logging. For Private (on-prem/VPC), retention is controlled by customer config (we do not access private logs).
- Alerting & escalation: alerts route to Console + optional webhook to SIEM; typical P1/P2 escalation follows our incident runbook with 15-min paging for P1. We will include runbook excerpt.

Attachments included in this message: monitoring_screenshots.zip (screenshots of Console alerting and per-route traces), kv_retention_policy.txt (excerpt with TTLs), redwood_fraud_detection_runbook.pdf (excerpt).

Let me know if you want numbers (avg alerts/day for a 100k MAU workload, false-positive rate) — I can pull metric snapshots.
